devline.flowCaption: How a run moves through devline. Implementation and review run once per task, side by side, so the number of agents follows the plan.
devline.flowAlt: Stages in order: brainstorm, plan, implement with a review for every task, documentation, deep review of the whole branch, then merge or iterate. You approve after the brainstorm, after the plan and at the end. Implement and review run one agent per task in parallel. A blocking review finding sends the task back to its implementer.
devline.flowEach: One agent per task, all tasks of a wave at once
devline.flowLoop: A blocking finding goes back to the implementer, then the task is reviewed again

agent.plan/planner: Owned files and tests per task
agent.implement/implementer: One per task, in its own worktree
agent.implement/debugger: When a build or test run fails

run.replan: After three blocking rounds the planner rewrites the approach
run.iterate: Iterate: back to the plan with what should change
run.hooks: Hooks on every command and file access

hook.validate-write: Denies reads of keys and .env files

run.srOptional: Only for UI changes, skipped otherwise.
run.srKinds: Three kinds of building blocks: skills are the stages and the commands. Agents do the work a skill hands them. kb-skills are knowledge the agents load. A skill can run on its own.

terms.text: The standard notation for business processes: tasks, decisions and the paths between them, drawn as a diagram that a process engine can run.
Business analysts draw the processes, developers make them run on an engine such as Operaton, and the people in charge of a process monitor it.
My text notation for the same diagrams. An `if` replaces the drawn diamond, so developers write, review and merge a process like any other code.

method.title: The round-trip test
method.lede: The evaluation checks whether a real process comes back unchanged from a trip into BPMNscript and back. Each model went through these steps:

steps.title: Collect real models
steps.text: BPMN files from public GitHub projects, listed in a dataset by Türker et al. (2022). None of them are mine.

steps.title: Deploy the original
steps.text: Operaton has to deploy the original, or the model doesn't count.

steps.title: Import into BPMNscript
steps.text: The importer turns the model into code, or refuses it with an error that names the construct it can't write, such as a connector to an external service.

steps.title: Compile back to BPMN
steps.text: The compiler turns that code into a new BPMN file.

steps.title: Compare and deploy again
steps.text: The new file has to match the original in its flows, conditions, task settings and names, and Operaton has to deploy it.

method.refused: {count} refused, each with an error that names the construct
method.lost: {count} come back different, or the tool fails on them
